query: Reported superconducting high-entropy alloys are dominated by Nb-Ta matrices, while other studies concern titanium-rich systems based on heavy transition metals and partly ordered systems. Consequently, these precedents do not establish what controls superconductivity in high-entropy alloys outside the best-studied material classes. Within the defining constraint of a solid solution containing at least five elements at no less than 5 atomic percent each, what governs superconducting behavior in such an uncharacterized high-entropy alloy, and why? State one testable mechanistic hypothesis, a controlled comparison against the starting material, predicted observations relative to the baseline, applicable boundary conditions, the earlier evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The superconducting behavior in high-entropy alloys is governed by the presence of a body-centered cubic (bcc) phase, which is responsible for the superconducting properties, while other phases such as hexagonal close-packed (hcp) are non-superconducting.

generation.intervention: Addition of scandium (Sc) to the alloy
generation.conditions: Solid solution containing at least five elements at no less than 5 atomic percent each
generation.mechanism: Superconductivity originates from the bcc phase fraction, which demonstrates identical superconducting parameters as the bcc parent alloys
generation.predicted_outcome: The high-entropy alloy will exhibit superconducting behavior if it contains a bcc phase, regardless of the presence of other phases
generation.baseline: Non-superconducting behavior in the absence of a bcc phase

generation.uncertainty: The exact role of the hcp phase in the superconducting behavior of the alloy is unclear

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a high-entropy alloy with a bcc phase and measure its superconducting properties
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy does not exhibit superconducting behavior, the hypothesis is falsified

## Abstract
AbstractIn this study, we investigate the scandium-containing Sc-Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr system of refractory high-entropy alloys (HEAs). Using the arc-melting method, we synthesized nine equimolar alloys (five 4-, three 5- and one 6-component), with all of them containing Sc. The alloys were characterized by XRD, electron microscopy and EDS, while superconductivity was investigated via electrical resistivity, specific heat and the Meissner effect. The results were compared to the parent Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr refractory HEAs, forming a single-phase body-centered cubic (bcc) structure and quite homogeneous microstructure. The addition of Sc produces a two-phase structure in the Sc-Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys, with one phase being bcc and the other hexagonal close-packed (hcp). The hcp phase absorbs practically all Sc, whereas the Sc-poor bcc phase is identical to the bcc phase in the Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr parent system. Upon the Sc addition, the microstructure becomes very inhomogeneous. Large bcc dendrites (10–100 µm) are homogeneous in the central parts, but become a fine dispersion of sub-micron precipitates of the bcc and hcp phases close to the edges.
